under the target, so the change ships a flag that does not fire on the one session it was built for, and a rule shipped
to every project quotes an unmeasured number (Working style: verify against the real system before writing a claim into
docs or code). The value of the target is the owner's pick (Q1); the wrong basis is not.

details: For the owner. How it works: relay report divides the front's API requests by the owner's turns and flags the period
when the ratio is over a constant. Live example: the session the item calls wasteful made 534 requests over 47 turns
(11.4), close to today's 10.5. Answers: (a) keep requests per turn and set the target to 11 (flags the bad session and
9 of 22 sessions; simple); (b) keep 15 (flags only the extreme sessions, 5 of 22; the bad session passes);
(c) flag on context read per owner turn instead (closer to cost; one more figure, needs a new measure). Recommendation
(a), resting on the 22-session measure above. Size: 5 minutes for (a) or (b), ~30 for (c).
evidence: $ python3 -I scratchpad/measure_front.py 10   (interactive sessions >= 5 turns, requests per turn, sorted)
failing_case: Live, 10 days, 22 interactive sessions with 5+ owner turns: requests per turn 2.2 .. 42.7, median ~10; the item's bad
session 0cc68fe0 is 11.4, this front session 3207dc59 10.5. Target 15 flags 5 of 22 and not 0cc68fe0; target 11 flags
0cc68fe0 and 9 of 22; a context-weighted figure (requests x context read, per owner turn) would rank sessions by what
the item says costs money (60% of the front's cost was context reads).
fix_hint: Ask the owner; then set the constant and its comment from the answer (F1).
pass_cases: 1. The owner's pick is written beside FRONT_REQUESTS_PER_TURN_TARGET with the measured numbers it rests on.
2. Under the pick, 0cc68fe0 is flagged if the owner wants the item's bad case flagged.
reason: Question for the owner, not answered: which target flags the front (11 flags 0cc68fe0 and 9 of 22 sessions; 15 flags 5 of 22 and not it; or a context-weighted figure). The fixer's 30-day table agrees: no measure separates the session. Recommendation unchanged: ask the owner; if the aim is a cost signal, use context read per turn.
findings.summary: which target the front-requests flag uses: requests per owner turn barely separates the bad session (11.4) from a typical one (median ~10)
